solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Note landlord giving party in the States

definitions.note: names a member of the party, as a noun

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
a publican is the landlord who keeps a pub

explanation.surface: A musical landlord hands over a note at an American political gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note' could be any letter A to G, but here it is the sol-fa RE.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the two main US political parties is the GOP, whose members carry this name.

clue.text: Champing at the bit, gunners round African country

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, the army's gunners
a ring is a round shape
Togo is a small country in West Africa

explanation.surface: Artillerymen circling an African state are impatient to get going.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: an eager horse chews its bit, so champing means impatient and keen to start.

clue.text: Boxer winning, turning over leader of group

indicators.note: turning over flips the word for winning so it reads backwards in this down light

parts.note: a team that is up is ahead, winning

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A fighter on top in the bout gets knocked over by the gang's boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxer' suggests a fighter, but it means the slang for a pugilist.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang abbreviation: a pugilist, a fist-fighter, is shortened to this three-letter word.

clue.text: Obvious victory for former PM

parts.note: a bald statement is plain, obvious
a win is a victory

explanation.surface: A former prime minister's landslide was a clear win.
explanation.walkthrough: Stanley Baldwin was British Prime Minister three times between the wars.
explanation.definitionFit: Stanley Baldwin led three Conservative governments in the 1920s and 1930s.

clue.text: Almost transfix a horned antelope

indicators.note: almost means the word for transfix stops one letter short of its end

parts.note: to impale is to pierce through, transfix

explanation.surface: A hunter nearly spears an antelope with horns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' drops the final E of IMPALE.
explanation.definitionFit: This African antelope, a springing grazer, has lyre-shaped horns on the male.

clue.text: A model upset Greek author

indicators.note: upset turns the word for model over, so in a down light it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: to pose is to model for an artist

explanation.surface: An artist's sitter is distressed by an ancient Greek writer.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Greek storyteller credited with the famous animal fables.

clue.text: Have to get in cheeses and chocolate cakes

indicators.note: to get in places the word for have within the cheeses

parts.note: Bries are soft French cheeses
to own something is to have it

explanation.surface: Someone must stock up on cheese and chocolate cake.
explanation.definitionFit: Brownies are small dense chocolate cakes cut into squares.

clue.text: Right about front of gallery being magnificent

indicators.note: about means the word for right goes around the next letter

parts.note: real means right as an intensifier, as in a right or real mess

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A conservative critic calls the gallery's facade splendid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right' is not R here: REAL (as in 'a right fool', 'a real fool') goes 'about' G.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something fit for royalty is splendid, grand and magnificent.

clue.text: Dad's attempt to make choux, perhaps

parts.note: pa is dad, so Dad's gives PA'S
a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: Father has a go at making choux buns in the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'choux' is the definition by example, marked by 'perhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: choux is the light dough used for eclairs and profiteroles.

clue.text: A Roman Catholic had once misled Anglican church official

indicators.note: misled means led astray, so these letters wander into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Catholic priest once deceived a senior clergyman of the Church of England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misled' rearranges A, RC, HAD and ONCE.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Church of England this senior cleric ranks just below a bishop and assists with diocesan administration.

clue.text: Down in Devon, a pageant

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the words that follow, running across them

explanation.surface: Something feels down at a West Country festival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Down' looks like a mood or a direction, but it means soft fluffy surface fibre; the letters hide in 'DevoN A Pageant'. Devon is an English county.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words name the soft raised fibres or fluff on the surface of cloth.

clue.text: Spoiled parties, a freeloader

indicators.note: spoiled means ruined, so these letters are wrecked and reassembled

explanation.surface: A gatecrasher who never contributes ruined the parties.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a sponger who lives off others without giving anything back.

clue.text: Want right resolution

parts.note: to will something is to want or wish it
a power is a right or authority to act

explanation.surface: Wishing for the correct decision.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: determination or strength of mind to carry something through.

clue.text: Absolute ruler's harangue after Troy gutted

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: after sends the word for harangue behind the gutted city
gutted means the insides of Troy are removed, leaving its outer letters

parts.note: a rant is a harangue

explanation.surface: A despot's tirade after the sacking of Troy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gutted' means emptied of insides, so only the first and last letters of Troy stay.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a despot or autocrat holding unchecked power.

clue.text: Apparition of one consumed by anger

indicators.note: consumed by means swallowed up within the word for anger

parts.note: wrath is great anger
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A vision of someone eaten up with rage.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a ghost or spectre, especially one seen shortly before or after death.

clue.text: Add insult to injury, having part in bankruptcy

indicators.note: in places the word for part inside the word for bankruptcy

parts.note: ruin is financial collapse, bankruptcy
a bit is a part

explanation.surface: Being involved in someone's financial collapse only makes things worse.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to keep reminding someone of a failure, making a bad situation worse.

clue.text: Study after odds become bigger

indicators.note: after puts the word for study behind the odds

parts.note: SP is the starting price, the odds at the start of a race
to read a subject is to study it

explanation.surface: Reading up on the betting makes the stakes grow.
explanation.walkthrough: SP, the starting price, is the bookmaker's odds when a race begins.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to extend or expand over a wider area.

clue.text: Dished roast up in GB bar

indicators.note: in puts the rearranged letters inside the abbreviation for Great Britain
dished means served up in a different form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A roast is served up in a British pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dished' rearranges ROAST UP to ASTROPU, which goes 'in' GB.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a pub with a bar that also serves high-quality restaurant food.

clue.text: Steps taken by odd graduate

parts.note: rum is old British slang for odd or strange
a BA is a Bachelor of Arts graduate

explanation.surface: A peculiar graduate takes steps on the dance floor.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: steps of a dance, here the Cuban ballroom dance.

clue.text: Novel, second by ambassador

parts.note: HE, His Excellency, is the title of an ambassador

explanation.surface: An ambassador's newest book comes a close runner-up.
explanation.walkthrough: H. Rider Haggard's novel 'She' is the definition; 'Novel' looks like an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: H. Rider Haggard's 1887 adventure story about an immortal queen bears this title.

clue.text: Terribly misty approaching end of office block

indicators.note: terribly means badly, so these letters are jumbled
the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Fog nears an office block and makes things dreadfully murky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terribly' rearranges MISTY; the end of office adds E.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as verbs: to obstruct, thwart or hinder.

clue.text: Subject suggested by principal in charge

parts.note: top means chief, principal

explanation.surface: A theme proposed by the head teacher who runs things.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the theme or matter under discussion.

clue.text: Climbing to dump mine

indicators.note: climbing means the word for dump goes upwards in this down light, reading backwards

parts.note: a tip is a rubbish dump

explanation.surface: Scaling a rubbish heap to fly-tip waste down a mine.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a coal mine or the shaft sunk to reach it.

clue.text: Stuffing not put back in bear

parts.note: padding is soft stuffing

indicators.note: put back means the word not is turned around

explanation.surface: A teddy whose stuffing hasn't been replaced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put back' turns NOT into TON. Paddington is the fictional bear from Peru found at the London station.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Michael Bond's marmalade-loving children's book bear from darkest Peru.
